(I took the joke from a Jimmy Kimmel comment and adapted it to #gamergate. I would say it fits.Lol.) Hello interweb peeps. I just created my account and this is my very first time posting pretty much anything on the internet (other than the occasional FB status and the selfie that you somehow justify to yourself that is worth posting for some reason! Lol. Hope you guys like it, but in general I would like to hear some thoughts on this. The two main concerns I was left with in the aftermath of #gamergate are in general the following. I’ll try to summarize as much as possible. In general I don’t see this getting too long, but the first point does require some explaining to do. 1.- Journalism as a whole, personal views, and agendas. My main concern is this: I love games. I very much do so. But, if you ask me to put it into context, I could live with saying that it is not extremely important. The world would be much bleaker and boring without it, true. but still, not really a priority for the world and humanity general. So, that puts games “journalism” easily quite a few steps below it in importance. Now, with that said: the fact that a few dimwit, narcissistic, not very successful, pseudo journalists could launch a campaign the size of “gamers are dead”, and that most of the mainstream media bought the narrative without doing so much as a lazy attempt to fact check, RRRREALLY makes me wonder: what are other sectors of journalism distorting, or flat out hiding, in areas were the stakes are much higher (E.Gr.: military, government, corruption, drug trafficking, human trafficking, etc.)? For this point, bear in mind that the legendary level morons that are acting like nothing was said about journalistic integrity launched the “gamers are dead” (very similar wording, lingo, and concept) within THE SAME DAY. These geniuses couldn’t even wonder if it would be suspicious publishing all those articles on THE SAME DAY. That’s where my shit-o-meter goes crazy. NONE of them thought: “hey game journo pros: I wonder if it would be better to release these articles with a day or two in between, to make it look like an opinion floating around the gaming community, you know?... - NO! we run it all the same day, damn it!” I mean: how laughable is it that ALL the articles were realized within the same day (aug 28. I personally think that fact should be highlighted as much and as frequently as possible). In general, for what I read for myself, these are very average people at most, in best case scenario. Many of them are obviously just shy of the average I.Q. and with deeply rooted prejudices that they don’t hold back on projecting everywhere and try to make it pass as journalism. Well, these had the balls to launch the whole “gamers are dead” campaign because something that happened on the industry was not of their liking, or didn’t fit their agendas, or their complexes, or they just felt like sweeping it under the rug. So, what are more relevant, delicate, dangerous areas of journalism distorting? It was a real eye opener in terms of suspecting how much we really don’t know at all about what’s happening in general.

2.- the bare face attitude that they assumed once being pointed out their irregularities.

I mean, they are definitely uncomfortable about it, but they are more actively trying to “burn everything to the ground” because they got caught, rather than correct behaviors, assume responsibility, and move on (hell, even fading away slowly and quietly would be less embarrassing than this whole scandal). And here, once again the rest of the media behavior is worrisome, to say the least. Only a couple of outlets did some level of diligence regarding the whole #gamergate. I have read a lot of them, and most of them would benefit a lot from checking the “knowyourmeme” [http://knowyourmeme.com/memes/events/gamergate] and the way they compiled and documented the events regarding the whole affair. They are just merely stating them, with files that back up what they found out, and just with that they are doing far more and far better journalism than most of the mainstream media combined. I still haven’t fully wrapped my head around the serious implications of that. I would recommend you at this point to let it sink in for a moment... Anyways, other than some small corrections in code of ethics here and there in gaming websites, have we actually seen positive changes in the aftermath?

ELI5: How do you change the subverses listed at the top of the page on Voat?

Go to whatever subverse you want to add or remove. Look to your right and subscribe/unsubscribe. Then click on settings (the gear next to your status on the top right). Look for the option to Replace top menu bar with my subscriptions and then check it.

My "option to Replace top menu bar with my subscriptions" was enabled by default. I'll add to your advice by saying that on the right side of front page there are 6 buttons, 2 blue(red for night mode) on top of 4 white(grey). The bottom most white button says Explore Voat. Clicking it will give you a list of the most popular subverses in an easy to subscribe to format.This is the best way i have found to customize your front page.

Good add.

Let me add to your advice and say that on all pages you can click on the far right of the top bar where it says "more" to get to the same list.
